source: Alxatib & Pelletier (2011) The psychology of vagueness: borderline cases and contradictions
finding: People accept 'tall and not tall' and 'neither tall nor not tall' for a middling-height man far more than for clear cases. Acceptance peaks at the borderline.
numbers: N=76 SFU undergraduates (63.2% native English). 20 True/False/Can't tell items, 4 per suspect, 5 suspects (5'4, 5'11, 6'6, 5'7, 6'2), no fillers, random order. At 5'11: 'both' true 44.7%, false 40.8%; 'neither' true 53.9%, false 42.1%.
limits: One population, one adjective (tall), picture stimuli. Can't-tell option was offered (9.2% at 5'11 for 'tall').
agent_relevance: People tolerate both-and-neither descriptions of a borderline case. A scaffold should not treat a flagged contradiction as an automatic error state.

source: Alxatib & Pelletier (2011) The psychology of vagueness: borderline cases and contradictions
finding: The same people who accept 'neither' often accept 'both'. Gap and glut readings are not cleanly separate groups.
numbers: At 5'11: of those saying 'neither' is true, 53.7% also said 'both' true, 31.7% false, 14.6% can't tell. Of those saying 'both' true, 64.7% also said 'neither' true. 32.4% of 'both'-true people also said 'tall' false and 'not tall' false. McNemar-Bowker test neither vs both: 8.04, p<0.05 (as reported by Egre et al.).
limits: Correlational. Could reflect one 'borderline' response strategy rather than a real logic. 'Both' true while 'tall' false and 'not tall' false means conjunction elimination is not applied.
agent_relevance: Humans do not apply conjunction elimination to a contradiction they accept. A paraconsistent reasoner does the same.

source: Alxatib & Pelletier (2011) The psychology of vagueness: borderline cases and contradictions
finding: Assent is asymmetric: people deny 'not tall' more than they deny 'tall' at the borderline, so they prefer denial to assent.
numbers: At 5'11: 'tall' true 46.1%, false 44.7%; 'not tall' true 25.0%, false 67.1%. Can't tell 9.2% and 7.9%. 'Tall' true rose from 1.3% (5'4) to 98.7% (6'6).
limits: Authors read this as a bias that errors of commission are graver than omission. Other readings exist (context shift, pragmatic strengthening).
agent_relevance: Default stance under conflict is to withhold both, not to affirm both. Gaps (hold off) are more natural than gluts.

source: Egre, Zehr et al. (2016 draft; 2018 chapter) Are gaps preferred to gluts? A closer look at borderline contradictions
finding: Serchuk, Hargreaves and Zach (2011) data as tabulated by Egre et al.: borderline conjunctions are mostly rejected; borderline disjunctions are accepted far more.
numbers: N=350 responses per sentence. 'x is P and x is not P': true 66, false 195, other 89. 'x is P and it is not the case that x is P': true 25, false 247, other 78. 'Either P or not P': true 113, false 137, other 100. 'P or it is not the case that P': true 141, false 88, other 121. Fisher tests p<1e-10 and p<1e-16.
limits: Second-hand table (original Mind & Language paper not opened). Vignette ('somewhere between clearly rich and clearly non-rich'), six-option forced choice. Glut acceptance is NOT robust: about 19% and 7% true for conjunctions.
agent_relevance: A weaker replication of glut acceptance: tolerance depends strongly on wording (sentential negation, 'it is not the case that'). Wording of conflict prompts matters.

source: Egre, Zehr et al. (2016 draft; 2018 chapter) Are gaps preferred to gluts? A closer look at borderline contradictions
finding: Ripley (2011) found no preference between gap and glut descriptions on a 1-7 scale, with acceptance highest at middling circle-square distances.
numbers: 7 circle-square pairs at varying distance, 1-7 agree scale, elided vs non-elided forms. Stimulus C (middle) got the highest assent for both types. Exact means shown only in a figure.
limits: Second-hand summary of Ripley's data. No gap/glut preference here conflicts with Alxatib-Pelletier and the Egre study.
agent_relevance: Different paradigms give different gap/glut preferences. Do not hard-code one.

source: Egre, Zehr et al. (2016 draft; 2018 chapter) Are gaps preferred to gluts? A closer look at borderline contradictions
finding: New online experiment: both 'and' (glut) and 'neither' (gap) descriptions of borderline cases are accepted above false controls, but 'neither' is preferred to 'and'.
numbers: N=148 Mechanical Turk participants, none excluded. Mixed-effects logistic regression, baseline Neither: intercept 3.60; And -4.35 (z=-8.98, p<2e-16); control False -10.52 (z=-14.56); control True +4.24 (z=2.59, p=.0096). Order effect: 'and' acceptance fell from about 50% to about 35% when judged after the antonym block. Adjective effect: 'and' acceptance rose from about 37% to about 66% (object-oriented before human-oriented).
limits: Only relative gradable adjectives; absolute adjectives (full, dry) not tested. Large order and adjective moderators. Participants were asked to imagine middle-range cases.
agent_relevance: Gaps are preferred to gluts, yet both are used. Supports keeping 'unknown' and 'conflicted' as distinct allowed states.

source: Egre, Zehr et al. (2016 draft; 2018 chapter) Are gaps preferred to gluts? A closer look at borderline contradictions
finding: Authors argue the pattern shows a preference for incompleteness over inconsistency, explained by local pragmatic strengthening, not belief in true contradictions.
numbers: More than 37% of participants accepted 'neither' and 'and' together (authors' estimate); no 'can't tell' option offered. They reject the 'can't tell' explanation because it cannot explain acceptance of 'and'.
limits: Competing explanations: contextualism (two occurrences of 'tall' read differently), strict/tolerant ambiguity, bipolar belief. Not resolved.
agent_relevance: Humans who 'accept contradictions' often mean a context shift. Check whether a conflict is a shift in standard before treating it as a clash of facts.

source: Cobreros, Egre, Ripley, van Rooij (2015) Pragmatic interpretations of vague expressions: strongest meaning and nonmonotonic consequence
finding: The pragmatic account (strict/tolerant meaning plus strongest meaning hypothesis) predicts the observed acceptance but keeps explosion valid under st-entailment.
numbers: Cites four experiments (Alxatib-Pelletier, Ripley, Serchuk, Egre) showing borderline contradictions acceptable. Reply by Alxatib, Pagin, Sauerland (2013) shows the pragmatic account predicts wrong interpretations for some disjunctions and proposes a fuzzy-logic semantics that drops conjunction elimination.
limits: Theory paper; no new data. Two competing models: pragmatic (classical logic kept) vs semantic (non-explosive).
agent_relevance: Live dispute: treat contradiction as a meaning shift, or reason non-explosively. Both fit the data.

source: Cobreros, Egre, Ripley, van Rooij (2015) Pragmatic interpretations of vague expressions: strongest meaning and nonmonotonic consequence
finding: Under the semantic reply, assertability of 'T(a) and not T(a)' does not license 'T(a)': conjunction elimination is relaxed.
numbers: Authors note explosion 'is predicted to be valid' under st-consequence, 'perhaps not as desirable as it may seem'.
limits: Authors' concern: the relation between assertion and inference is lost.
agent_relevance: Directly relevant to S6: assert both, do not derive either from the pair.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025-26) Sound and complete neurosymbolic reasoning with LLM-grounded interpretations
finding: Bilateral factuality evaluation (ask separately whether a claim can be verified and whether it can be refuted; Belnap four values) raises macro-F1 over a unilateral true/false judge, but only by abstaining on inconsistent or uncertain cases.
numbers: N=400 items each from GPQA and SimpleQA derived sets, balanced. 6 judges (Llama 4 Maverick, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet; Scout, GPT-4o Mini, Haiku), 3 prompt types, 14,400 calls. Mean macro-F1 gain +0.062 (p<0.01), coverage change -0.456. GPQA flagship 0.699 vs 0.633; SimpleQA flagship 0.736 vs 0.657; distilled 0.608 vs 0.559 and 0.624 vs 0.570. Coverage 0.589/0.504 (GPQA flagship/distilled) and 0.584/0.499 (SimpleQA).
limits: Gain is on the answered subset only; coverage falls to roughly 50-59%. Negatives synthetically generated by GPT-4o Mini. Bootstrap SE about 0.01. Cost about twice the time and tokens.
agent_relevance: A conflict state costs about half the coverage. Use it as a trigger to gather evidence, not as a final answer.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025-26) Sound and complete neurosymbolic reasoning with LLM-grounded interpretations
finding: LLMs hold inconsistent knowledge often: gluts (verified AND refuted) are more common than gaps (neither).
numbers: Table 3 shares: flagship GPQA glut 0.301, verified-only 0.211, refuted-only 0.378, gap 0.110; distilled glut 0.299, gap 0.197. SimpleQA flagship glut 0.310, gap 0.106; distilled glut 0.301, gap 0.200. Gluts more frequent than gaps (p<0.05). The weak-Kleene 'error' value never occurred in 14,400 calls.
limits: Internal discrepancy: the later domain analysis (zero-shot, Table 14) reports GPT glut about 59.0%, much higher than Table 3 averages. Rates depend on prompt and setup. 2024-era models.
agent_relevance: A model asked to affirm and to deny the same claim will often do both. Asking both questions separately exposes conflict that one true/false question hides.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025-26) Sound and complete neurosymbolic reasoning with LLM-grounded interpretations
finding: Model families differ sharply in how they handle a claim and its negation: GPT models say yes to both, Claude models abstain more.
numbers: Zero-shot SimpleQA by family: GPT glut 59.0%, gap about 0.1%; Claude glut 19.6%, gap 30.4%; Llama glut 52.9%, verified-only 29.8%. By topic: video games glut 63.6%, sports 47.3%, history lowest 35.7% (SD 15.0 across models). Flagship-minus-distilled macro-F1 gap: bilateral 0.091 GPQA and 0.112 SimpleQA vs unilateral 0.074 and 0.087 (p<0.01).
limits: Descriptive; no human baseline. Prompts force a terminal VERIFIED/CANNOT VERIFY line.
agent_relevance: Conflict rate is a model property. Any 'hold both' operator needs per-model calibration; some models will manufacture conflict.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025-26) Sound and complete neurosymbolic reasoning with LLM-grounded interpretations
finding: A tableau reasoner on a medication-safety knowledge base localizes contradictions instead of exploding.
numbers: 228 asserted statements (28 rules, 200 ground facts, 16 drug classes) forward-chain to 712 inferred (940 total). 92 gluts detected: 25 opioids nonaddictive, 30 benzodiazepines nonaddictive, 11 antipsychotics, 11 beta-blockers safe in asthma, 7 fluoroquinolone-in-children (category breakdown partly garbled in extraction). 2 gaps. Theory stays satisfiable. Over 99% of runtime is LLM calls; tableau under 10 ms.
limits: Proof of concept; single judge (GPT-4o); two rules were deliberately wrong, so some detection is by design. No precision or recall against clinicians. End-to-end effect of LLM miscalibration left as future work.
agent_relevance: A contradictory set can be kept and queried, and each glut points to the faulty derived step. Maps onto S6 trace-back.

source: Bao, Fu, Witbrock (2025-26) Conflict-Aware Fusion: mitigating Logic Inertia in LLMs
finding: Rule-based reasoners collapse completely when a contradictory rule is injected: they keep deducing instead of halting.
numbers: Instance-level accuracy on base task 1.000 for BERT, Qwen2, TinyLlama; Variant 3 (contradiction injection) 0.000 for all; Variant 2 (essential rule deletion) 0.25-0.295; Variant 4 stacked laws Qwen2 0.645, TinyLlama 0.9925, BERT 1.000.
limits: Synthetic propositional benchmark with closed-world labels. 'Correct' means halt under a conservative semantics chosen by the authors, not a paraconsistent one. Small fine-tuned models.
agent_relevance: Models trained on deduction have no stop for contradiction. This is explosion-like failure in practice.

source: Bao, Fu, Witbrock (2025-26) Conflict-Aware Fusion: mitigating Logic Inertia in LLMs
finding: Frontier models also continue deducing after noticing a contradiction.
numbers: GPT-4o halts correctly on 56.0% of 800 contradiction test questions (44.0% continue); Gemma-3-4B-IT 43.9% (56.1% continue). Base accuracy GPT-4o 0.789, Gemma 0.580. Example: given {A->B, A, not B}, GPT-4o notes the inconsistency, then concludes B.
limits: The authors' 'correct' answer is a halt, which a paraconsistent reasoner would not require. Error analysis on stratified 200-row samples. Vendor and prompt specific.
agent_relevance: Verification and execution are compartmentalized. Add an explicit check step that gates deduction, and repeat it after each derived step.

source: Bao, Fu, Witbrock (2025-26) Conflict-Aware Fusion: mitigating Logic Inertia in LLMs
finding: A four-stage training fix (SFT with a verification preamble, DPO, invariance regularization, RL with symbolic reward) gets perfect halt-on-contradiction and transfers partly to natural-language NLI.
numbers: Fusion-Conflict (1.5B and Qwen3-8B): 1.000 on base, V2, V3. Qwen2-1.5B V3 ablation: SFT 0.210; CoT 0.510; RA-CoT 0.865; Fusion-LRA 0.972. Out of domain (Qwen2.5-0.5B): LogicNLI 58.5% (SFT), 65.2% (augmentation), 92.4% (no DPO), 98.2% (full); MNLI contradiction subset 34.1, 41.5, 78.3, 89.4%. Removing the preamble drops Qwen2 base accuracy to 0.525. Lean-4 check: 99.0% agreement on 105 classically derivable questions, 36.6% on 82 F cases.
limits: Training result, not a scaffold; our agent cannot train. Saturation on a synthetic test. Invariance regularization alone cut sensitivity from 1.0 to 0.47. V4-multi drops to 0.773 at 1.5B. Authors state paraconsistent resolution is out of scope.
agent_relevance: The verification-before-deduction preamble is what matters (0.525 without it). That is a prompt-level step a scaffold can copy.

source: Li, Raheja, Kumar (2024) ContraDoc: understanding self-contradictions in documents with LLMs
finding: Detecting an internal contradiction in a long document is hard for LLMs; GPT-4 is best and about matches humans.
numbers: 449 self-contradictory documents (news 158, wiki 150, story 141). Binary judgment accuracy: GPT-3.5 50.1%, GPT-4 53.8%, PaLM2 52.0%, LLaMA2 50.5%; GPT-4 recall 8.0% at 97% precision. Evidence hit rate (top-5): GPT-4 70.2%, GPT-3.5 42.8%, PaLM2 48.2%, LLaMA2 20.4% (random 16%).
limits: Contradictions inserted by GPT-4 and human verified. GPT-4 does better on wiki (82.0%) than story (62.4%). Weaker on contradictions needing nuance.
agent_relevance: The agent must first notice a conflict; direct yes/no detection is near chance, locating evidence is better.

source: Li, Raheja, Kumar (2024) ContraDoc: understanding self-contradictions in documents with LLMs
finding: On a 150-document human comparison, GPT-4 matches or beats humans; weaker models say 'yes, contradictory' too often but cannot point to evidence.
numbers: Humans: TP 18.0%, FP 6.7%, evidence hit 74.1%, real accuracy 26.7%. GPT-4: TP 20.0%, FP 4.7%, evidence hit 86.7%, real accuracy 34.7%. GPT-3.5: FP 15.3%, evidence hit 25.8%, 10.7%. Full dataset judge-then-find: LLaMA2 recall 95.0%, FP 37.6%, evidence hit 41.0%, real accuracy 13.8%; GPT-4 precision 88%, recall 39%, real accuracy 35.6%.
limits: Table text partly garbled by extraction; only rows read cleanly are given. 'Real accuracy' is the paper's own metric (yes plus correct evidence). Annotators: one per document.
agent_relevance: Require evidence for any conflict claim; a bare conflict flag is cheap and unreliable.

source: Fan, Li, Sun, Zhou (2025) Missing premise exacerbates overthinking
finding: Ill-posed questions with missing premises make reasoning models think far longer without noticing the problem; non-reasoning models do better.
numbers: MiP sets: 50 formulas, 300 SVAMP, 582 GSM8K, 58 MATH. Non-reasoning models need about 200 tokens on well-defined GSM8K vs about 1,000 for DeepSeek-R1 and 1,800 for QwQ-32B. Reasoning models' abstain rate on MiP-GSM8K roughly 10-56%; MiP-Formula response lengths up to about 12,900 tokens. GPT-o1 abstained best among reasoning models.
limits: Missing premise, not contradictory premise. Table extraction is messy, so ranges only. GPT-4o as judge. Overthinking spreads through distillation.
agent_relevance: Impasse analogue: when a premise is missing or conflicting, the agent loops. It needs a cheap early exit that names the gap or conflict.

source: Li, Li, Chang, Wu (2025) Don't take the premise for granted: PCBench
finding: LLMs seldom critique flawed or contradictory premises on their own; they need explicit prompts.
numbers: PCBench: 1,200 base problems (100 per error-difficulty combination), 3,600 total across three variants, 15 LLMs. Qwen3 non-thinking, 8B to 235B: critique rate with prompt (APCR) 59.9% to 70.0%; proactive rate (PPCR) 20.6% to 24.7%. Critique outputs are much longer: o3-mini PPCCR 3.90, APCCR 3.11; DeepSeek-R1 PPCCR 2.71. Auto-grader vs graduate students kappa 0.8921 (Qwen3-235B-thinking) and 0.7763 (GPT-4.1), 240 instances.
limits: Obvious contradictions are caught more than contradictory inferences, irrelevant-query distraction, or flawed solutions. Reasoning ability and critique ability are not consistently correlated.
agent_relevance: Detection must be an explicit step, not an expected spontaneous act.

source: Li, Li, Chang, Wu (2025) Don't take the premise for granted: PCBench
finding: Some reasoning models detect the contradiction internally but silently pick one side and answer.
numbers: DeepSeek-R1 case: it deliberates over '1/4 of a skein' vs '182 yards', then computes with 182 yards only and does not tell the user.
quote: it ultimately ignores the fractional information
limits: One qualitative case plus authors' general claim.
agent_relevance: Hidden resolution without disclosure. A paraconsistent scaffold should surface the conflict and carry both readings forward.

source: Chen, Chi, Wang, Zhou (2024) Premise order matters in reasoning with LLMs
finding: Reordering premises of a logically identical problem cuts LLM accuracy by over 30%, so reasoning is order-sensitive.
numbers: GPT-4-turbo and PaLM 2-L accuracy drops of up to 20-30% under shuffled premise order; Gemini 1.0 Pro also drops. Best when order matches the proof. New R-GSM benchmark also shows drops.
limits: Not about contradiction. Distracting rules amplify the effect.
agent_relevance: A held inconsistent set may be read differently by order; test the held conflict under two orderings.

source: Cheng (2025) Why cannot large language models ever make true correct reasoning?
finding: Position paper argues LLMs cannot reason correctly because classical implication permits irrelevant premises; wants relevant logic.
numbers: No experiments or numbers.
limits: Opinion; the claim that no LLM can be correct with certainty is untested.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence. Cite only as an argument that relevance-aware logic matters.

source: Alxatib & Pelletier (2011) The psychology of vagueness: borderline cases and contradictions; Egre, Zehr et al. (2016 draft; 2018 chapter) Are gaps preferred to gluts? A closer look at borderline contradictions
finding: Across four human experiments (Alxatib-Pelletier N=76, Ripley, Serchuk 350 per item, Egre N=148) glut acceptance at the borderline is above false controls in all, but varies widely with wording, order and adjective.
numbers: 'True' rate for glut sentences: 44.7% (A&P at 5'11), 18.9% and 7.1% (Serchuk conjunctions), about 35-50% and 37-66% depending on block order and adjective type (Egre).
limits: Between-study range of 7% to 66% shows weak robustness. All use vague predicates; none test genuine factual contradictions.
agent_relevance: Human tolerance of contradiction is about vagueness, not conflicting facts. Do not generalize to evidence conflict.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025-26) Sound and complete neurosymbolic reasoning with LLM-grounded interpretations; Bao, Fu, Witbrock (2025-26) Conflict-Aware Fusion: mitigating Logic Inertia in LLMs
finding: Two LLM works point in opposite directions: Allen keeps contradictions and abstains on them; Bao halts on them. Neither tests continued problem solving with the conflicting set.
numbers: Allen: coverage down about 46 points for +6.2 F1. Bao: halting gives 1.000 on synthetic V3 after training, GPT-4o untrained 0.560.
limits: No study found that measures task performance when an agent keeps a contradictory set alive versus forcing one choice. That is the direct S6 test and it is missing.
agent_relevance: Evidence gap. Our own runs where early candidates conflict are the only test.
